selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps, Switzerland

experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes
experiences.description: Ski across the world-famous Jungfrau ski region covering Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. With over 200km of groomed pistes suitable for all skill levels, families can enjoy beginner slopes alongside more challenging runs. Ski school lessons are available for children and beginners, making it an ideal full-day family adventure in the heart of the Bernese Oberland.

experiences.name: Glacier Paradise at Klein Matterhorn
experiences.description: Take the highest cable car in the Alps up to Klein Matterhorn at 3,883m for year-round glacier skiing and breathtaking panoramic views of the Matterhorn. Families can explore the Glacier Palace ice cave, enjoy snow tubing, and ski on pristine glacier snow. A truly unforgettable high-altitude experience that combines adventure with stunning Alpine scenery.

experiences.name: Family Snow Tubing and Sledding at Grindelwald
experiences.description: Experience the thrill of snow tubing and traditional Swiss sledding on dedicated family-friendly slopes in Grindelwald. The First Flieger zip-line and Trottibike snow scooters add extra excitement for older kids. This activity requires no skiing experience, making it perfect for younger children and non-skiers in the family while still delivering maximum winter fun.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience
experiences.description: Visit a traditional Swiss mountain restaurant (Bergrestaurant) for an authentic cheese fondue dinner paired with local Swiss wines and Rivella. Learn about the centuries-old tradition of Alpine cheese-making and enjoy raclette prepared tableside. Many mountain huts in the Engadin valley offer live folk music evenings, giving families a warm cultural immersion into Swiss Alpine heritage.
experiences.location: St. Moritz Old Town, Engadin Valley

experiences.name: Horse-Drawn Sleigh Ride Through Snowy Alpine Villages
experiences.description: Glide through snow-covered Alpine meadows and charming Swiss villages on a traditional horse-drawn sleigh ride. Wrapped in warm blankets, families are treated to stunning mountain vistas, frozen lakes, and the peaceful silence of the Swiss winter landscape. Many operators in the Engadin region offer routes past frozen Lake Silvaplana, making this a magical and uniquely Swiss family memory.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps, Switzerland

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 13:00, collect luggage and take the budget-friendly Swiss Federal Railway (SBB) train toward the Swiss Alps region. Purchase a regional day pass at the station for savings. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your room. Take a short orientation walk around the immediate resort area to get your bearings, spot nearby ski lifts, and enjoy your first views of the alpine scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest village on foot — browse local shops for affordable ski gear rentals and lift pass options for the week. Head to a cozy local restaurant or resort dining area for a welcome dinner. Rest early to recover from travel and prepare for a full Day 2.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a quick pastry and coffee at Zurich Airport (budget ~CHF 8-10)
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or pretzel from a train station kiosk or airport bakery (budget ~CHF 10-12)
meals.dinner: Local mountain restaurant — try Rösti (Swiss potato dish) or a hearty soup with bread. Look for 'Tagesmenü' (daily set menu) for best value (budget ~CHF 18-25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Swiss Travel Pass or regional ski-area transport pass at the airport or train station — it can save significantly on transport throughout the week. Confirm ski rental shop hours near the resort for Day 2 preparation. Pack layers as alpine temperatures in February typically range from -5°C to +2°C.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the nearest ski rental shop early (opens ~8:30 AM) to rent skis, boots, and poles for the week — weekly rentals are far cheaper than daily rates (budget ~CHF 30-40/day equivalent on a weekly deal). Purchase a beginner or family ski lift pass. Take a beginner ski lesson or a family group lesson offered by the resort ski school — group lessons are much more affordable than private ones (budget ~CHF 40-60 per person for a half-day group lesson).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hit the beginner and intermediate slopes with your family. Most Swiss Alpine resorts have dedicated family ski zones with gentle runs and magic carpet lifts for young children. Enjoy the wide-open snowy landscape and take plenty of photos. Take a mid-afternoon hot chocolate break at a mountain hut or self-service ski lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Return ski equipment to lockers, warm up at the resort. Walk to the village for a budget dinner. Browse the local supermarket (Migros or Coop, if available nearby) to stock up on snacks, breakfast items, and drinks to save money throughout the week.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered or resort continental breakfast — pick up bread, cheese, and yogurt from a local supermarket the evening before (budget ~CHF 5-8 per person)
meals.lunch: Self-service mountain restaurant on the slopes — soup, pasta, or a simple hot dish (budget ~CHF 15-20 per person)
meals.dinner: Village pizzeria or fondue restaurant — cheese fondue is a Swiss classic and surprisingly affordable when shared (budget ~CHF 20-28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ski school group lessons in advance online — they often sell out during peak February school holiday season. Children under 9 often ski free or at heavily discounted rates at many Swiss resorts. Apply sunscreen even on cloudy days — alpine UV reflection off snow is very strong.

day_by_day.morning: Full day of skiing on intermediate slopes. Start early (lifts typically open at 8:30-9:00 AM) to avoid crowds. Try a different sector of the ski area using your lift pass — explore blue (easy) and red (intermediate) runs. Families with young children can revisit the dedicated kids' snow park with fun obstacles and small jumps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic gondola or cable car ride to a higher elevation viewpoint for panoramic Alpine views — often included in the lift pass. Enjoy snowshoeing as an alternative activity for non-skiers in the family (snowshoe rentals ~CHF 10-15/day). Visit an igloo or snow sculpture display if available at the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski: Join the lively but free outdoor atmosphere at the base of the slopes — many resorts have free live music or entertainment at slope-side bars. Opt for a budget drink (local beer or mulled wine/Glühwein ~CHF 5-8) and soak up the atmosphere without overspending.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort — muesli, fruit, and hot drinks prepared in-room or from supermarket supplies (budget ~CHF 4-6 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket supplies eaten on the mountain or in a free picnic area (budget ~CHF 6-8 per person)
meals.dinner: Resort or village restaurant — try Älplermagronen (Swiss alpine mac and cheese with potatoes and bacon) or Bratwurst with bread (budget ~CHF 18-24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wednesday is often 'family day' at many Swiss ski resorts with special activities for children. Check the resort's weekly program board or website for free events. Keep your lift pass safely stored — replacements can be expensive.

day_by_day.morning: Take a break from skiing and explore a nearby Alpine village on foot or by local bus (use your transport pass). Visit a traditional Swiss church, browse artisan shops, and admire classic wooden chalets. Many villages have free walking maps available at the tourist information office.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try tobogganing (sledding) — one of the most fun and affordable winter activities in Switzerland. Many resorts have dedicated toboggan runs with sled rentals for ~CHF 10-15. Alternatively, try a free-to-use public sledding hill near the village. Families with children will love this activity. Return to the resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local indoor swimming pool or wellness center if available at or near the resort for an affordable wind-down (many Swiss resorts have public pools, ~CHF 10-15 per person). Alternatively, enjoy a family board game night or movie in the resort lounge area.

meals.breakfast: Village bakery breakfast — fresh croissants, bread rolls, and coffee at a local Bäckerei (budget ~CHF 8-12 per person)
meals.lunch: Village café or supermarket deli counter — pick up a warm sandwich, soup, or salad (budget ~CHF 10-15 per person)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal in-room if kitchen facilities are available, or visit a Migros or Coop supermarket hot food counter for ready-made meals (budget ~CHF 10-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Thursday is a great mid-trip rest day to give legs a break from skiing. Toboggan runs are often open until late evening with lighting — check local resort information for night sledding sessions which are a magical experience for families.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the slopes refreshed after the rest day. Friday mornings are typically less crowded than weekends. Focus on improving skiing technique — consider a short 2-hour group refresher lesson for the family (budget ~CHF 30-40 per person). Explore any ski runs not yet attempted during the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a guided or self-guided snowshoe trail through a quiet forested Alpine area — many trails are free to use with just the cost of snowshoe rental. Enjoy the peaceful silence of the snow-covered forest, spot wildlife tracks, and take in unspoiled mountain scenery away from the busy ski runs.
day_by_day.evening: Treat the family to a slightly more special Friday dinner — try a traditional Swiss Raclette dinner (melted cheese over potatoes and pickles). Many restaurants offer Raclette as a shared table experience. This is a cultural highlight and still budget-friendly when shared.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered continental breakfast with supermarket supplies — bread, cold cuts, cheese, juice (budget ~CHF 5-7 per person)
meals.lunch: Mountain hut lunch — a warming bowl of Gerstensuppe (barley soup) or Minestrone with bread, widely available on the slopes (budget ~CHF 12-16 per person)
meals.dinner: Traditional Raclette restaurant in the village — shared Raclette set for the table (budget ~CHF 25-35 per person, worth the splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings in Alpine villages often have local events, live folk music, or craft markets — check the village notice board or tourist office for free entertainment. Book the Raclette restaurant in advance as Friday evenings fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Full final ski day — make the most of your lift pass. Try any remaining ski runs on your bucket list. Consider a ski safari — a guided route that takes you across different sectors of the ski area, often offered free by resort ski hosts. Saturdays can be busier so start early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in a free or low-cost family snow activity at the resort base — many resorts organize free snow sculpting competitions, family races, or ski demos on Saturdays. Alternatively, visit a nearby frozen lake for free ice skating (check safety conditions locally) or simply enjoy a leisurely snowball fight and snowman building with the family.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner celebration — visit the best-value restaurant identified during the week. Enjoy a final Swiss meal together as a family. After dinner, take a moonlit walk through the snowy village, enjoy the Alpine night sky (minimal light pollution makes stargazing spectacular), and pack bags for the journey home.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or local café — fuel up well for the last full ski day (budget ~CHF 8-12 per person)
meals.lunch: On-mountain self-service restaurant — pasta or soup for energy (budget ~CHF 14-18 per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a village restaurant — try Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (veal in cream sauce with Rösti) or a hearty Swiss stew. Share a bottle of local Swiss wine for a treat (budget ~CHF 28-38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Return ski rental equipment by the end of the day if your rental period ends today — returning early in the afternoon avoids queues. Purchase any Swiss souvenirs today — local supermarkets like Coop and Migros sell Swiss chocolate, cheese, and small gifts at far lower prices than tourist shops.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a final breakfast with any remaining supermarket supplies or a quick café stop. Take one last walk around the resort or village to soak in the Alpine scenery and take final photos. If time permits before departure, visit a local church for Sunday morning bells — a quintessential Swiss Alps experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel by Swiss Federal Railway (SBB) back toward Zurich Airport or your departure hub. The scenic train journey through the Alps is itself a highlight — sit on the right side of the train for the best mountain views. Arrive at the airport with ample time (recommend 2.5-3 hours before international departure).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. Reflect on an amazing budget Alpine adventure with the family.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast using remaining supplies or a quick bakery stop in the village (budget ~CHF 6-10 per person)
meals.lunch: Train station or airport food court — Coop to Go or Migros at the station offer affordable sandwiches and hot food (budget ~CHF 12-15 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Swiss trains run on a precise schedule — confirm your train times the evening before and allow extra time for luggage. The SBB app (free download) provides real-time train schedules and platform information. Keep CHF 10-20 cash per person for any last-minute airport expenses. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights and accommodation): CHF 150-220 per adult per day including lift passes, ski rentals, meals, and activities — significantly lower than typical Swiss Alpine trip costs by using group lessons, self-catering, and public transport.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange ground transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Swiss Alps. Transfer via train or pre-booked shuttle (approx. 2–3 hours depending on exact resort location).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your Beachfront accommodation. Take a leisurely orientation walk around the resort and nearby village to get your bearings. Visit the resort's ski rental shop or local ski hire center to book equipment for the week — reserve ski passes for the Jungfrau Region in advance to save time.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at the resort's main restaurant or a nearby mid-range Alpine restaurant. Enjoy a warm, hearty Swiss meal to recover from travel. Early night recommended to rest up for a full first ski day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or at the airport during transit.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Zurich/Geneva airport — try a Swiss bakery sandwich or a Migros/Coop airport outlet (CHF 10–15).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant or a local Alpine Stube — try Rösti with Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (sliced veal in cream sauce) or a hearty Alpine soup. Budget approx. CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tip: Book ski passes and equipment rental online before arriving to avoid queues. Confirm resort transfer options (train to Grindelwald or Wengen is scenic and recommended). Pack layers — Alpine evenings drop well below freezing in February.

day_by_day.morning: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes — Start your first full ski day at Grindelwald First or Kleine Scheidegg. The Jungfrau ski region covers over 200km of groomed pistes across Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. Beginners can take ski school lessons (book through resort), while intermediate and advanced skiers can explore blue and red runs with stunning Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the Jungfrau slopes. Take the Männlichen gondola for panoramic ridge views and enjoy a mid-afternoon run down to Grindelwald. Families with younger children can rotate between gentle beginner slopes and a short break at a mid-mountain sun terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Horse-Drawn Sleigh Ride Through Snowy Alpine Villages — After returning skis, enjoy a magical twilight or early-evening horse-drawn sleigh ride through snow-covered Alpine meadows and the charming village of Grindelwald. This classic Swiss experience is perfect for families and takes approximately 45–60 minutes.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at the resort — fuel up with muesli, Swiss bread, cold cuts, eggs, and fresh juice (included or CHF 18–25 if separate).
meals.lunch: Mountain lunch at a Bergrestaurant on the slopes — try Älplermagronen (Alpine mac and cheese with applesauce) or a hot soup with bread. Budget CHF 20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a cozy local restaurant in Grindelwald village — try Raclette melted tableside or a fondue starter. Mid-range budget CHF 35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Rent ski helmets for all family members — mandatory for children under 14 in most Swiss resorts. Apply high-SPF sunscreen even on cloudy days; Alpine UV reflection off snow is intense. Sleigh rides should be pre-booked — contact the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Paradise at Klein Matterhorn — Take an early departure toward Zermatt (approx. 2–2.5 hours by train via Visp — a scenic and manageable day trip). Ride the highest cable car in the Alps up to Klein Matterhorn at 3,883m. The views of the Matterhorn and surrounding glaciers are breathtaking. Year-round glacier skiing is available here on wide, gentle slopes — perfect for all skill levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski the glacier slopes at Klein Matterhorn. The runs here are generally wide and less crowded than lower resorts. Explore the ice cave carved into the glacier (included with cable car ticket). Take photos at the summit viewing platform with the iconic Matterhorn backdrop before descending back to Zermatt village.
day_by_day.evening: Explore car-free Zermatt village before heading back. Browse the charming Alpine shops and warm up with a Glühwein (mulled wine) at a village bar. Return to the resort by train — arrive back by 20:00–21:00.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — grab a packed snack or thermos coffee for the train.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Bergrestaurant at Klein Matterhorn or at the Trockener Steg mid-station — try Berglinsen (mountain lentil soup) or a cheese toastie. CHF 25–35 per person.
meals.dinner: Quick dinner in Zermatt before the train back — try a mid-range pizzeria or Swiss bistro in the village. Zermatt has excellent options at CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Altitude warning: Klein Matterhorn at 3,883m can cause mild altitude sickness — stay hydrated, ascend slowly via cable car stages, and avoid overexertion on arrival. Children under 8 should consult a doctor before high-altitude exposure. Check Swiss rail schedules the night before — trains to Zermatt require a change at Visp.

day_by_day.morning: Family Snow Tubing and Sledding at Grindelwald — Take a well-deserved break from skiing and head to Grindelwald's dedicated family snow tubing and sledding area. This activity is perfect for all ages and skill levels. Snow tubing lanes are fast and thrilling, while the traditional Swiss toboggan (Schlittelbahn) runs offer a classic Alpine experience. Grindelwald's First Flieger zip line is also nearby for adventurous older children and adults.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue with family activities at Grindelwald — try the First Cliff Walk by Tissot, a suspended walkway offering dramatic cliff-edge views (open weather permitting in winter). Alternatively, rent snowshoes from the resort and take a guided or self-guided snowshoe trail through the forest above Grindelwald for a peaceful winter nature experience.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience — Book an authentic fondue dinner at a traditional Bergrestaurant or mountain chalet. This cultural dining experience includes a guided introduction to Swiss cheese varieties, traditional Moitié-Moitié fondue (Gruyère and Vacherin), local bread, and a glass of Swiss Fendant white wine for adults. A memorable family evening.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — relaxed start, no early departure needed today.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at the snow tubing area's on-site café or a nearby village bakery — hot chocolate, sandwiches, and fresh-baked pretzels. CHF 15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Traditional Swiss fondue dinner at a Bergrestaurant — budget CHF 40–60 per person including fondue, bread, salad, and a drink. Book in advance as popular spots fill quickly.

day_by_day.notes: Snow tubing and sledding require waterproof outerwear and gloves — ensure children are fully equipped. The fondue experience is the highlight cultural activity of the trip; request a table by the fireplace for the full Alpine ambiance. Non-skiers or those with ski fatigue will particularly enjoy today's itinerary.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes — Head to Mürren, the car-free cliff-top village accessible by cable car and train from Lauterbrunnen. Mürren offers some of the most dramatic skiing in Switzerland with views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau directly in front of you. Advanced skiers should try the legendary Schilthorn Inferno run (the longest downhill race course in the world at 15km).
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski the Schilthorn area — ride the cable car to 2,970m and enjoy the 007 James Bond panorama restaurant (Piz Gloria, featured in 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service'). Take a break for a coffee or hot chocolate at Piz Gloria with 360-degree rotating views. Descend back to Mürren on varied terrain before heading back to the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort — use the spa or wellness facilities if available (many Alpine resorts offer saunas, hot tubs, and steam rooms). Light dinner at the resort bar or lounge — ideal recovery evening before the final full ski day.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — early start for the Mürren cable car.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Piz Gloria (Schilthorn summit) — a unique dining experience at 2,970m. Expect mid-to-upper mid-range pricing CHF 30–45 per person for the iconic location.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at the resort lounge or a nearby village pizzeria/bistro — pizza, pasta, or a light Alpine platter. CHF 25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Mürren is car-free — access is by cable car from Stechelberg or train/cable car via Lauterbrunnen and Grütschalp. Allow extra travel time (approx. 1 hour from Grindelwald). The Schilthorn cable car has its own ticket pricing separate from the Jungfrau ski pass — check combined pass options at the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Final Ski Day — Wengen Slopes and Lauberhorn Area. Wengen is another car-free Alpine village and home to the famous Lauberhorn World Cup downhill ski race. Explore the Wengen–Männlichen area for long, sweeping intermediate runs with stunning valley views. Families can enjoy the gentle Wengen nursery slopes while advanced skiers tackle the Lauberhorn race course sections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski back down to Grindelwald via the Kleine Scheidegg connecting runs — a classic Alpine traverse that showcases the best of the Jungfrau region. Return ski equipment to the rental shop. Spend the late afternoon exploring Grindelwald village — visit local artisan shops for Swiss chocolate, cheese, and Alpine gifts to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner — Celebrate the trip with a special dinner at a highly-rated local restaurant. Opt for a full Swiss Alpine menu — start with a cheese soup, main course of Alpine beef or lake trout, and finish with Meringue with double cream (a Grindelwald specialty). Toast with a local Swiss wine or Appenzeller schnapps.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — full fuel-up for the last ski day.
meals.lunch: Mountain lunch at Kleine Scheidegg station restaurant — a historic railway station café with panoramic Eiger views. Try the daily Alpine special. CHF 25–35 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a recommended local Alpine restaurant — budget CHF 50–70 per person for a full celebratory meal with drinks. Ask the resort concierge for current top-rated local recommendations.

day_by_day.notes: Return all rental equipment today to avoid late fees. Purchase Swiss chocolate and specialty items (Gruyère, Appenzeller, Raclette cheese to travel) at local shops — vacuum-sealed cheese travels well. Book a taxi or transfer for tomorrow's departure tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — enjoy a slow resort breakfast and take a last scenic walk through the Alpine village. If time permits, take a final snowshoe stroll or simply sit at a café terrace with a coffee and soak in the mountain views. Pack and prepare luggage for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and begin transfer to the airport. Depending on your flight time, you may have time for a stop in Bern (Switzerland's capital, approx. 1 hour from Grindelwald) or Zurich city center for a brief sightseeing stop — the Old Town (Altstadt) and Bahnhofstrasse are walkable from the main station. Head to the airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — allow ample time at the airport for check-in, security, and Swiss duty-free shopping (excellent chocolate, watches, and Swiss Army knives). Board your return flight.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — take your time and enjoy the last Alpine morning views.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a café in Bern or Zurich if time allows, or at the airport — try a final Swiss cheese sandwich or Brezel. CHF 15–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Swiss trains run precisely on schedule — plan your transfer to the airport with at least 30 minutes buffer. Zurich Airport (ZRH) has excellent shopping and dining if you arrive early. Ensure ski equipment bags (if you rented your own gear) are within airline baggage allowances. Keep CHF cash for any last-minute tips or small purchases — not all mountain vendors accept cards.

day_by_day.afternoon: Resort Check-In & Orientation — Settle into your Beachfront suite at Aegean Bliss Resort. Meet your dedicated concierge for a personalized welcome briefing, review your week's itinerary, and explore the resort's world-class amenities including the heated outdoor pool, spa, and ski-in/ski-out access. Take a leisurely stroll around the resort grounds to acclimate to the altitude.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome Dinner at the Resort's Signature Restaurant — Enjoy a lavish multi-course Alpine welcome dinner at the resort's flagship fine-dining restaurant. Savor dishes such as pan-seared venison, truffle risotto, and a curated selection of Swiss wines. End the evening with a fireside cognac in the resort's private lounge.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or pre-arrival)
meals.lunch: Light refreshments and snacks during the private transfer — curated charcuterie box and Swiss chocolates prepared by the resort
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort Signature Restaurant — 5-course Alpine tasting menu with wine pairing; expect CHF 200–300 per person

day_by_day.notes: Altitude acclimatization is important on Day 1. Keep hydration high and avoid strenuous activity. Concierge will assist with ski rental fittings and equipment bookings for the week. Confirm all activity reservations this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes — Begin your Alpine ski adventure with a guided private ski session across the legendary Jungfrau ski region, covering Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. A certified private ski instructor will tailor the morning run to all family members' skill levels, from beginner-friendly blue runs to expert black pistes. Enjoy over 213 km of pristine groomed slopes with breathtaking Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continued Skiing & Family Snow Tubing at Grindelwald — After a mountain lunch break, transition to the Family Snow Tubing and Sledding experience at Grindelwald. Dedicated family-friendly slopes offer exhilarating snow tubing lanes and traditional Swiss wooden sled runs. All safety equipment is provided; private guides ensure maximum fun and safety for younger guests.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience — Descend to a traditional Swiss Bergrestaurant (mountain restaurant) for an authentic cheese fondue dinner. Experience the time-honored ritual of melting Gruyère and Emmental cheeses over an open flame, accompanied by crusty bread, charcuterie, cornichons, and a bottle of Fendant white wine. Live accordion music adds to the cozy Alpine atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh pastries, smoked salmon, Alpine cheeses, eggs to order, fresh juices, and Swiss coffee
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant on the Jungfrau slopes — hearty Rösti with mountain herbs, Bratwurst, warm Alpine soup, and hot chocolate; expect CHF 60–90 per person
meals.dinner: Traditional Bergrestaurant Fondue Experience — classic cheese fondue, raclette station, and Swiss dessert platter; expect CHF 100–150 per person

day_by_day.notes: Ski equipment rental and lift passes for the Jungfrau region should be pre-booked through the resort concierge. Jungfrau Top Ski Region pass covers all interconnected lifts. Dress in warm, waterproof layers. Snow tubing is suitable for children aged 5 and above.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Paradise at Klein Matterhorn — Embark on the crown jewel of Alpine experiences: a ride on the highest cable car in the Alps to Klein Matterhorn at 3,883 meters. Ascend through dramatic vertical landscapes to the Glacier Paradise, where year-round glacier skiing awaits on a vast, pristine snowfield. A private mountain guide will lead the family safely across the glacier, sharing geological and historical insights about this iconic peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Glacier Skiing & Ice Palace Exploration — Continue glacier skiing on the wide, gentle slopes perfect for all family members. Visit the famous Ice Palace carved deep within the glacier — a magical labyrinth of ice sculptures and frozen chambers. Enjoy a warm break at the panoramic summit restaurant before the cable car descent back to the valley.
day_by_day.evening: Horse-Drawn Sleigh Ride Through Snowy Alpine Villages — As dusk settles over the Alps, board a beautifully decorated traditional horse-drawn sleigh for a romantic and enchanting glide through snow-covered Alpine meadows and charming Swiss villages. Wrapped in faux-fur blankets with mulled wine (hot chocolate for children) in hand, this is a quintessential Swiss winter fairy-tale experience.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — Eggs Benedict with smoked trout, bircher muesli, freshly baked croissants, and a Champagne mimosa option
meals.lunch: Matterhorn Glacier Paradise Summit Restaurant — panoramic views paired with Alpine goulash soup, cheese tart, and warm strudel; expect CHF 70–100 per person
meals.dinner: Intimate dinner at a premium Zermatt village restaurant post-sleigh ride — rack of lamb, truffle potato gratin, and a curated Valais wine selection; expect CHF 180–250 per person

day_by_day.notes: Klein Matterhorn cable car tickets sell out quickly; pre-book through the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance. The summit temperature can be -15°C or lower — full thermal ski gear, goggles, and sun protection (SPF 50+) are essential. The horse-drawn sleigh ride lasts approximately 45–60 minutes and must be booked in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury Spa & Wellness Morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — Dedicate the morning to rest and rejuvenation at the resort's world-class spa. Enjoy a family wellness session including Alpine herb steam baths, heated indoor/outdoor pools, and individual signature massages (hot stone, deep tissue, or aromatherapy). Children can enjoy a dedicated junior spa treatment or supervised activity in the resort's kids' club.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Snowshoeing Excursion in the Alpine Backcountry — Accompanied by a certified Alpine guide, embark on a private snowshoeing journey through untouched backcountry terrain surrounding the resort. Discover hidden valleys, frozen waterfalls, and panoramic ridge viewpoints inaccessible to regular ski traffic. The pace is leisurely and tailored to the family, making it both adventurous and accessible.
day_by_day.evening: Private Igloo Dining Experience — Enjoy an exclusive private dinner in a custom-built igloo on the resort grounds or a nearby mountain venue. A personal chef prepares a 4-course gourmet Alpine menu inside the intimate, candlelit ice structure, featuring dishes like foie gras, Swiss beef tenderloin, and a chocolate fondant dessert. Stargazing from the igloo entrance caps the magical evening.

meals.breakfast: In-room premium breakfast delivered to your suite — Continental spread with Swiss pastries, seasonal fruit platters, freshly pressed juices, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Light spa cuisine at the resort's wellness café — quinoa bowls, avocado toast, Alpine herb teas, and fresh smoothies
meals.dinner: Private Igloo Dinner — 4-course gourmet menu with wine pairing curated by the resort's sommelier; expect CHF 300–450 per person (exclusive experience)

day_by_day.notes: Spa bookings should be made the evening before to secure preferred time slots. Snowshoeing equipment is provided by the guide service. The igloo dining experience is weather-dependent and should be confirmed with the concierge by midday. Children's menus are available for the igloo dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Advanced Skiing Day on Jungfrau Region — Return to the Jungfrau ski region for a full-day advanced skiing experience. Today, explore the more challenging red and black runs of Mürren and Wengen with your private ski instructor. The Schilthorn run from Mürren — made famous by the James Bond film 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service' — is a highlight not to be missed. Enjoy the dramatic 360-degree panorama from the revolving Piz Gloria restaurant at the summit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski Picnic & Free Skiing — The resort concierge prepares a gourmet mountaintop picnic basket with artisan sandwiches, Swiss cheeses, cured meats, macarons, and a thermos of hot soup. Enjoy this in a scenic slope-side shelter. Spend the afternoon skiing freely at your own pace, exploring your favorite runs from earlier in the week.
day_by_day.evening: Gala Dinner at a Michelin-Starred Alpine Restaurant — Conclude the ski-intensive day with an extraordinary dining experience at a Michelin-starred restaurant in the region (such as Restaurant Memories in Bad Ragaz or a comparable local establishment). A private transfer is arranged. The menu showcases modern Alpine cuisine — think venison tartare, pike-perch with alpine herbs, and a deconstructed Toblerone dessert.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at the resort — made-to-order omelettes, smoked salmon blinis, Swiss granola, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Gourmet mountaintop picnic prepared by the resort chef — artisan charcuterie, aged Alpine cheeses, fresh baguette, chocolate truffles, and hot soup thermos
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred Alpine restaurant — 7-course tasting menu with wine pairing; expect CHF 350–500 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Schilthorn/Piz Gloria run requires intermediate to advanced skiing ability. Beginners in the family may prefer to enjoy the revolving restaurant and cable car experience without skiing this section. Michelin-starred restaurant reservation must be made well in advance — the concierge should book this on Day 1 of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Private Ice Skating & Winter Sports Sampler — Enjoy a private session at a premium outdoor or covered ice skating rink in the region. A professional skating coach provides personalized instruction for all family members. Follow this with a brief introduction to cross-country skiing (Langlauf) on a scenic groomed track through the forest — a gentler, meditative contrast to downhill skiing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swiss Cultural Village Tour & Shopping — Board a private chauffeured vehicle for a curated tour of a nearby authentic Swiss Alpine village (such as Grindelwald or Wengen). Visit a local artisan workshop, browse luxury Swiss watch boutiques, and explore specialty shops for handcrafted wooden toys, Swiss chocolate, and premium souvenirs. Stop at a historic village chapel for a quiet cultural moment.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Horse-Drawn Sleigh Ride & Private Fondue Party — Revisit the magic of the Swiss Alps with a farewell evening horse-drawn sleigh ride at sunset, followed by a private fondue and raclette party hosted in a reserved private dining room at the resort. The resort chef prepares multiple fondue varieties — classic cheese, Bourguignonne (meat), and chocolate — with premium accompaniments and a curated selection of Swiss wines and spirits.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast at the resort — smoked salmon, caviar blinis, freshly baked viennoiseries, and seasonal berries with cream
meals.lunch: Lunch at a charming village café during the cultural tour — Älplermagronen (Alpine macaroni), Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), and apple strudel; expect CHF 50–80 per person
meals.dinner: Private Fondue & Raclette Farewell Party at the resort — unlimited cheese fondue, Bourguignonne, chocolate fondue, and a Swiss wine and schnapps selection; expect CHF 200–280 per person

day_by_day.notes: Saturday markets in Alpine villages offer exceptional local produce and handcrafted goods — ideal for last-minute premium gifts. The private fondue party can be themed and decorated upon request through the concierge. Confirm the sleigh ride timing to align with the golden hour sunset for the best photographic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final Sunrise Ski Run & Summit Breakfast — Rise early for one last magical ski run as the sun rises over the Jungfrau peaks, painting the snow in shades of gold and rose. A private guide leads the family on a gentle, scenic morning descent chosen for its panoramic beauty rather than technical challenge. Conclude with a summit breakfast at a mountain restaurant — warm croissants, hot chocolate, and Alpine jams with a view that will last a lifetime.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure, Packing & Resort Farewell — Return to the resort for a final spa session or pool time. Pack and prepare for departure. The concierge arranges luggage handling and assists with any last-minute purchases or arrangements. Enjoy a farewell afternoon tea in the resort lounge — finger sandwiches, Swiss pastries, and a selection of fine teas and coffees.
day_by_day.evening: Private Luxury Transfer to Airport/Departure — A chauffeured premium vehicle departs the resort at a time coordinated with your outbound flight schedule. Enjoy a final scenic drive through the Swiss Alps, reminiscing about the week's extraordinary experiences. The resort provides a parting gift — a curated Swiss hamper with artisan chocolates, cheese, and a personalized photo book of your Alpine adventure.

meals.breakfast: Summit mountain restaurant breakfast — warm croissants, Alpine berry jams, Swiss cheese selection, hot chocolate, and espresso with panoramic Jungfrau views
meals.lunch: Farewell à la carte lunch at the resort's main restaurant — seasonal risotto, pan-seared Alpine fish, and a dessert of the day; expect CHF 80–120 per person
meals.dinner: Not applicable — departure transfer; resort provides a gourmet travel snack box for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Coordinate checkout time and transfer schedule carefully with the concierge on Day 6. The resort's Swiss hamper farewell gift should be requested in advance if specific items are preferred. Ensure all ski rental equipment is returned by morning. Keep one carry-on bag accessible for the summit breakfast morning — full luggage can be stored with the concierge from the night before.
